correctness.rationale: Normal equations yield G(Py)=(B/S)|sum c_i y_i|. Real-response coarea reduces the induced functional norm to all binary cuts; rearrangement makes a final segment optimal at each cardinality. Differentiability of all-pair G at the strictly ordered design and equality at the fixed input t force c proportional to index ranks, proving the arithmetic-grid iff condition. Direct arithmetic sums establish sufficiency. Differentiation of cut maxima yields the two sided cusp and positivity unless the perturbation is affine. Exact rational exhaustive small-cut computations, two-input tests, and explicit 28/25 witness were run as corroboration; unlimited n and real grids follow from the displayed proof, not a finite test.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus and primary literature queries compared induced pairwise-Gini norms, equivalence to centered-slope dual cut norm, and stronger Hilbert and L-infinity projector results. value.rationale: A standard least-squares projector is nonexpansive in Euclidean distance, but its exactly computed stability in the natural all-pair Gini variation depends sharply on the sampling geometry. The result completely classifies grids with Gini nonexpansivity, constructs exact counterexamples outside that class, identifies all norming binary cuts and computes a positive first-order irregularity penalty on both sides. These are structural robustness statements for sampled affine fitting, not isolated small numerical improvements.
